semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ}: its parallel was mentioned at the beginning of al-Raʿd. The pointing with «تلك» is to what the sūra contains, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. It was also said: it is a pointer to the earlier Books. The indefiniteness of «قرآن» is for magnification.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رُّبَمَا}: «رُبَّ» has two views. One: that it is a preposition (ḥarf jarr); the Kufans, Abū l-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash] and Ibn al-Ṭarāwa claimed that it is a noun. Its meaning is fewness (taqlīl) according to the well-known view. It was also said that it denotes abundance. It was also said that it denotes abundance in places of boasting, as in his saying:
2922 - 0- فيا رُبَّ يومٍ قد لَهَوْتُ وليلةٍ ... بآنسةٍ كأنها خطُّ تِمْثالِ (How many a day and night have I whiled away with a charming girl, as though she were the outline of a statue)
and it has been answered that this is to make a parallel few. The proofs of these views belong to grammar. It has many dialects, the best known of which is «رُبَ» with ḍamma, doubled or lightened; Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read with the second. And «رَبَ» with fatḥa, doubled and lightened, and «رُبْ» and «رَبْ» with ḍamma and fatḥa and sukūn in both. The tāʾ of feminine gender is attached to all of these, and with the tāʾ Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read: «رُبَّتَما». When the tāʾ is attached to it, sukūn and fatḥa are both allowed on it, as in «thummata» and «lāta», so the forms multiply. It has many rules, among them: the requirement that it stand at the head [of the clause]; among them that its genitive object be indefinite, and his saying:
292 - 3- رُبَّما الجامِلِ المُؤَبَّلِ فيهمُ ... وعَنَاجيجُ بينهنَّ المهَارى (How many a herd of camels is among them, and swift mounts, among which are riding camels)
is a poetic necessity in the transmission of the one who put «الجامِل» in the genitive. It also governs in the genitive a pronoun that requires explanation by an indefinite noun after it, in which dual, plural and feminine forms of the noun suffice in place of dual, plural and feminine forms of the pronoun, as in his saying:
292 - 4- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ورُبَّه عَطِباً أَنْقَذْتُ مِنْ عَطَبِهْ (... and how many a man in peril have I rescued from his peril)
Agreement, as in «رُبَّهما رجلين», is rare. At times what is annexed to the pronoun of its genitive object is conjoined to it, as in «رُبَّ رجلٍ وأخيه». Is it necessary that its genitive object be described, and that what is attached to it be in the past? There is disagreement; the sound view is that this is not necessary. Among instances of it without a description is the saying of Hind:
292 - 5- يا رُبَّ قائلةٍ غداً ... يا لهفَ أمِّ مُعاويهْ (O how many a woman will say tomorrow: Alas for the mother of Muʿāwiya!)
and among instances of the future is his saying:
292 - 6- فإنْ أَهْلَِكْ فربَّ فتىً سيبكيْ ... عليَّ مهذَّبٍ رَخْصِ البَنانِ (If I perish, how many a refined youth, soft of fingertip, will weep over me)
and her saying «يا رُبَّ قائلةٍ غداً», the verse, and the saying of Sulaym:
292 - 7- ومعتصمٍ بالحيِّ من خشية الرَّدى ... سيُرْدى وغازٍ مُشْفِقٍ سَيَؤُوب (How many a one who seeks refuge with the tribe for fear of death will perish, and a fearful raider will return)
for the particle of extension [of time] and «غداً» restricted the two to the future.
And «ما» in «رُبما» admits two aspects. The more apparent: that it is the enabling one (al-muhayyiʾa), meaning that «رُبَّ» is specific to nouns, so when «ما» came it enabled its entry on verbs. A parallel was mentioned earlier with «inna» and its sisters. It also restrains it from governing, as in his saying:
292 - 8- رُبَّما الجامِلُ المُؤَبَّلُ. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
in the transmission of the one who put it in the nominative, as happened with the kāf of comparison. The second: that «ما» is an indefinite noun described by the clause following it, and the returning pronoun to «ما» is omitted, its implied form being: «رُبَّ شيءٍ يَوَدُّه الذين كفروا» (how often a thing that those who disbelieved wish for).
And His saying: {يَوَدُّ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: whoever does not require that what is attached to it be past needs no interpretation; whoever does require that says: because what is awaited in the reports of Allah the Exalted is certain to happen, He expressed it in the past to confirm its occurrence, like His saying {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1] and the like.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ}: «لو» may be the one of prevention (imtināʿiyya), and in that case its answer is omitted, its implied form being: "if they had been Muslims they would have been glad of that," or "they would have been delivered from what they are in." The object of «يَوَدُّ» is omitted on this implication, that is: "Those who disbelieved will often wish for deliverance"; the preventive clause indicates it.
The second: that it is maṣdar-forming, according to those who hold that, as was explained in al-Baqara. In that case this maṣdar is the object of the wishing, that is: "they wish for their being Muslims," if we make «ما» a restraining one; and if we make it indefinite, «لو» and what falls within its scope is a badal (substitute) of «ما».

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذَرْهُمْ}: no past is used for this except rarely, «تَرَكَ» sufficing in its place; rather, the imperfect is used from it, as in {وَيَذَرُهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. An instance of the past is his saying, peace be upon him: «ذَرُوا الحبشة ما وَذَرَتْكم» ("Leave the Abyssinians alone as long as they leave you alone"). Similar is «دَعْ» and «يَدَعُ»; «وَدَعَ» is said only rarely, and «ما وَدَعك» has been read with lightening, and they recited his saying:
292 - 9- سَلْ أميري ما الذي غيَّرهْ ... عن وصالي اليومَ حتى وَدَعَهْ (Ask my master what has changed him toward me today, such that he has left [me])
And {يَأْكُلُواْ} is jussive as the answer to the imperative. It was mentioned earlier that «تَرَكَ» and «ذَرْ» may be in the sense of «ṣayyara» (to make), and on this the second object is omitted, that is: «ذَرْهُمْ مُهْمِلين» (leave them neglected); and «يأكلوا» is not the second object, nor a ḥāl, since it would have to be nominative.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ}: there are several aspects in it. The first, which is the apparent one, is that it is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and then you have two considerations. One: that you make the ḥāl the preposition and its genitive noun alone, and «كتابٌ» is nominative by it as an agent. The second: that you make the preposition phrase a fronted predicate, with «كتاب» a mubtadaʾ and the clause a ḥāl; and this ḥāl is inseparable.
The second: that the wāw is redundant, and he supported this by the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla «إلا لها» without it. But redundancy is not easy.
The third: that the wāw enters the clause that serves as an adjective, for emphasis. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The clause serves as an adjective of «قرية», and by analogy this wāw should not intervene between them, as in His saying {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 208]. It intervenes only to emphasize the attachment of the adjective to the thing described, as you say: «جاءني زيد عليه ثوبُه» and «جاءني وعليه ثوبُه»." Abū l-Baqāʾ, the Exalted, followed al-Zamakhsharī in that, and he had said so before in al-Baqara at His saying, the Exalted: {وعسى أَن تَكْرَهُواْ شَيْئاً وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ} [verse 216].
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "We do not know any grammarian who said this, and I recall that Ibn Jinnī preceded the two of them to that." Then the Shaykh said: "It is built on the permissibility of what follows «إلا» being an adjective, and they have forbidden that. Al-Akhfash said: «No separation is made between the adjective and the thing described by «إلا»». Then he said: as for «ما جاءني رجلٌ إلا راكبٌ», on the implication «إلا رجلٌ راكب», there is ugliness in it, because you make the adjective like the noun." Abū ʿAlī said: "You say «ما مررتُ بأحدٍ إلا قائماً», with «قائماً» a ḥāl, and you do not say «إلا قائمٍ», because «illā» does not intervene between the adjective and the thing described." Ibn Mālik said, having mentioned what al-Zamakhsharī held in «ما مررت بأحدٍ إلا زيدٌ خيرٌ منه», that the clause after «إلا» is an adjective of «أحد»: "It is a position not known from any Basran or Kufan, so no heed is paid to it," and he declared false his statement that the wāw intervenes to emphasize the attachment of the adjective to the thing described.
I say: al-Zamakhsharī's statement is strong in terms of analogy, for the adjective is like the ḥāl in meaning, even if there is a difference between them in some respects. Just as the wāw enters the clause that serves as a ḥāl, so it enters it when it serves as an adjective. What he offered as its parallel in the other verse, His saying {إِلاَّ لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ}, also strengthens it, as does the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla mentioned earlier.
Mundhir ibn Saʿīd said: "This wāw is the one that indicates that the state after it, in wording, is in time before the state preceding the wāw, and from it is His saying, the Exalted: {حتى إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا} [al-Zumar: 73]."

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مِنْ أُمَّةٍ}: the agent of «تَسْبِقُ», and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. It was construed on the wording of «أمَّة» in His saying «أجلَها», so it is singular and feminine; and on its meaning in His saying {وَمَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ}, so it is plural and masculine. What is attached to «يَسْتأخِرُون» is omitted, its implied form being «عنه», since the context indicates it and since it falls as a verse ending.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying, the Exalted: {نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذكر}: the majority read «نُزِّل» doubled and passive; Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نَزَلَ» lightened and active.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَّوْ مَا}: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) like «hallā», and it also functions as a particle of prevention due to existence, just as «lawlā» alternates between these two meanings. The difference between them is known: the urging one is followed only by a verb, overt or latent, as in his saying:
293 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . لولا الكَمِيَّ المُقَنَّعَا (... why do you not [strike] the armoured, helmeted warrior)
while the preventive one is followed only by nouns, in wording or in implication, according to the Basrans. And his saying:
293 - 1- ولولا يَحْسَبُون الحِلْمَ عَجْزاً ... لَمَا عَدِمَ المُسِيْئُون احتمالي (Were they not to count forbearance as weakness, the wrongdoers would not have lacked my tolerance)
is interpreted, against the Kufans. Among instances of «لَوْما» as a particle of prevention is his saying:
293 - 2- لَوْما الحياءُ ولوما الدينُ عِبْتُكما ... ببعضِ ما فيكما إذ عِبْتُما عَوَري (Were it not for modesty and were it not for religion, I would have reproached you both for some of what is in you, since you reproached me for my blemish)
They differed over it: is it simple or compound? Al-Zamakhsharī said: «لو» is compounded with «لا» and with «ما» for two meanings, whereas «هل» is compounded only with «لا» alone, for urging. They also differed over «لوما»: is it a base form in itself, or a derivative of «لولا», with the mīm substituted for the lām, as in their saying «خالَلْتُه» and «خالَمْته», so he is «خِلِّي» and «خِلْمي», that is: my friend? They also said «استولى عليَّ كذا» and «استومَى عليه» in a [single] sense? — a well-known disagreement. This clause of urging indicates the answer of the condition that follows it.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَا نُنَزِّلُ الملائكة}: Abū Bakr read «ما نُنَزِّل» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and fatḥa on the nūn and on the zāy, doubled, as a passive, with «الملائكةُ» nominative because it stands in the place of its agent. This agrees with His saying: {وَنُزِّلَ الملائكة تَنزِيلاً} [al-Furqān: 25], and with the fact that they are sent down only by the command of Allah, so someone other than they is the one who sends them down, and that is Allah the Exalted.
[Translator's note: the source writes the opening of Abū Bakr's reading as «ما نُنَزِّل» although it then describes ḍamma on the tāʾ; the intended form is evidently «ما تُنَزَّلُ». I have translated the description as written.]
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read with ḍamma on the nūn, fatḥa on the second [nūn], and kasra on the zāy, doubled, as an active verb of the Magnifier [the plural of majesty], who is the Creator, the Exalted, with «الملائكةَ» accusative as its object. It agrees with His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ الملائكة} [al-Anʿām: 111], and suits His saying before that, {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا} [al-Ḥijr: 4], and His saying after it, {إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا} [al-Ḥijr: 9], and the expressions of magnification that follow. The rest of the Seven read «ما تَنَزَّلُ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, the nūn and the zāy, doubled, with «الملائكةُ» nominative as the agent. The original is «تَتَنَزَّل» with two tāʾs, one of which is omitted, and its explanation was given earlier at {تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 152] and the like. It agrees with His saying {تَنَزَّلُ الملائكة والروح فِيهَا} [al-Qadr: 4].
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ما نَزَلَ» lightened, as an active, with «الملائكة» nominative as the agent, like His saying {نَزَلَ بِهِ الروح الأمين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193].
His saying: {إِلاَّ بالحق}: it may be attached to the verb before it, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent or the object, that is: "bound up with the truth." Al-Zamakhsharī made it an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "a sending down bound up with the truth."
His saying: «إَذَنْ»: al-Zamakhsharī said: «إذن» is a particle of answer and consequence, because it is an answer to them, and the consequence of the condition is implied, its implied form being: "And had We sent down the angels, they would not have been granted respite, and their punishment would not have been delayed."

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying, the Exalted: {نَحْنُ}: either a mubtadaʾ (subject) or an emphasis (tawkīd); it cannot be a separator (faṣl) because it does not fall between two nouns. The pronoun in «له» refers to the Reminder (al-dhikr), and this is the apparent view. It was also said: to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرْسَلْنَا}: its object is omitted, that is: "We sent messengers before you." So «مِنْ قبلك» may be attached to «أَرْسَلْنَا», or to an omitted element as an adjective of the omitted object.
And {شِيَعِ الأولين}: al-Farrāʾ said: "It is an annexation of the thing described to its description; the original is «في الشِّيَع الأولين», like «صلاة الأُولى» and «جانب الغربيّ»." The Basrans interpret it by omission of the thing described, that is: «في شِيَع الأممِ الأوَّلين», «جانب المكانِ الغربي», «صلاة الساعةِ الأولى».

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a narration of a past situation, because «ما» does not enter on an imperfect unless it is in the position of the ḥāl, nor on a past unless it is close to the ḥāl." What he mentioned is the more frequent in their speech, but it has come in conjunction with an imperfect intended for the future, as in His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ مَا يَكُونُ لي أَنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِن تِلْقَآءِ نفسي} [Yūnus: 15], and they recited the verse of al-Aʿshā in praise of the Prophet ﷺ:
293 - 3- له صَدَقاتٌ ما يَغِبُّ نَوالُها ... وليس عطاءُ اليومِ مانِعَه غَدا (He has gifts whose bounty never lapses, and today's giving does not prevent his giving tomorrow)
and the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
293 - 4- أودَى بَنِيَّ وأَوْدَعُونيْ حَسْرة ... عند الرُّقَادِ وعَبْرةً ما تُقْلِعً (My sons perished and left me a sorrow at sleeping-time and a tear that never ceases)
His saying: {إِلاَّ كَانُواْ}: this clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يَأتِيهمْ». It may also be an adjective of «رسول», in which case there are two aspects regarding its position: genitive in respect of the wording, and nominative in respect of the position; and if it is a ḥāl, it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَذَلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ}: the kāf may be nominative in position as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: «الأمرُ كذلك» (the matter is thus), with «نَسْلُكُه» resumptive. It may also be accusative in position: either an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: «مثلَ ذلك السَّلْكِ ونحوِه نَسْلُكُه» (in the like of that insertion We insert it), that is, We insert the Reminder; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied maṣdar.
The hāʾ in «نَسْلُكُه» may refer back to the Reminder (al-dhikr), and this is the apparent view. It was also said: it refers to the mockery. It was also said: to polytheism.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
The hāʾ in {بِهِ} may refer back to the three that preceded; and the interpretation of its referring to mockery and polytheism is: "they do not believe because of it." It was also said: to the Messenger; and it was said: to the Qurʾān. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a ḥāl, that is: they do not believe, mocking." I say: it is as though he made «به» attached to the omitted ḥāl, standing in its place; but this is rejected, because a preposition phrase, when it occurs as a ḥāl, an adjective, a relative clause or a predicate, is attached to an unrestricted existence, not a specific one, and likewise the adverbial.
The position of {لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} is accusative as a ḥāl, and it is possible that it has no position, because it is an explanation of His saying {كَذَلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ}.
And His saying {وَقَدْ خَلَتْ سُنَّةُ الأولين} is resumptive.
Al-salk: insertion. It is said: «سَلَكْتُ الخيطَ في الإبْرة» (I threaded the thread through the needle), and from it comes {مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ} [al-Muddaththir: 42]. It is said «سَلَكَه» and «أَسْلكه», that is: he strung it. The poet said:
293 - 5- وكنتُ لِزازَ خَصْمِك لم أُعَرِّدْ ... وقد سَلَكُوكَ في أَمْرٍ عَصِيْبِ (I was the close companion of your adversary, I did not flee, when they had drawn you into a hard affair)
and another said, with «أَسَلَكَ»:
293 - 6- حتى إذا أَسْلَكُوهمْ في قُتائِدَةٍ ... شَلاًّ كما تَطْرُدُ الجَمَّالةُ الشُّرُدا (until, when they drove them into a narrow pass, driving them as camel-herders drive the stray camels)

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فَظَلُّواْ}: it is the incomplete verb (nāqiṣa), and the pronoun in «فظلُّوا» refers to the disbelievers for whom the door was opened. It was also said: it refers to the angels. Al-Aʿmash and Abū Ḥaywa read «يَعْرِجون» with kasra on the rāʾ, which is in the dialect of Hudhayl for «عَرَجَ يَعْرِجُ», that is: he ascended.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سُكِّرَتْ}: Ibn Kathīr read «سُكِرَتْ» as a passive with the kāf lightened, and the rest of the Seven likewise, except that they doubled the kāf. Al-Zuhrī read «سَكِرَتْ» with fatḥa on the sīn and kasra on the kāf, light, as an active.
As for the first reading, it may be in the sense of the doubled one, for lightening suits both the little and the much. Both are taken from «السِّكْر» with kasra on the sīn, which is damming; so the meaning: our eyes were held back and blocked. It was also said: in the sense of "were disabled." It was also said: in the sense of "were seized." It was also said: in the sense of "were bewitched." It was also said: the doubled form is from the damming of water, and the lightened one is in the sense of "were bewitched." It was also said: the doubled form is from sikr of water with kasra, and the lightened one from sukr of drink with ḍamma.
It is well known that «سَكَر» is not transitive, so how is it built as a passive? Abū ʿAlī said: "It may have been heard transitive in the case of sight." What the verifiers among the language scholars said is that «سَكَرَ»: if it is from the intoxication of drink or the stillness of the wind, then the doubling in it is for transitivity; and if it is from the damming of water, then the doubling is for intensification, because it is transitive in the light form. For it is said «سَكَرَتْ الريح تَسْكُرُ سَكَراً» when it became still, and «سَكِر الرجلُ من الشراب سَكَراً» when he became still and did not carry out his need; these two are intransitive, so the doubling in them is for transitivity. And it is said «سَكَرْتُ الماءَ في مجارِيْه» when you stop it from flowing; this is transitive, so the doubling in it is for intensification.
As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, if it is from the damming of water, it is clear because it is transitive; and if it is from the intoxication of drink or the stillness of the wind, it is possible that the verb is used at times intransitively and at times transitively, like «رَجَع زيدٌ» and «رَجَعَه غيرُه», and «سَعَدَ» and «سَعَدَه غيرُه».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «وسُكِّرت»: they were bewildered, or held back, from sakar or sakr; and «سُكِرَتْ» was read lightened, that is: held back as a river is held back from flowing. So he made the doubled reading admit two meanings, and the lightened reading one meaning.
As for the reading of al-Zuhrī, it is clear, that is: "were disabled." It was also said: it is the reflexive of «أَسْكَرْتُ المكانَ فسَكِرَ», that is: I blocked it and it became blocked.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {جَعَلْنَا}: it may be in the sense of «خَلَقْنا» (We created), in which case the preposition phrase is attached to it; or in the sense of «صَيَّرنا» (We made), in which case its first object is «بُروجاً» and its second object is the preposition phrase, attached to an omitted element.
And «للناظرين» is attached to «زيَّنَاها». The pronoun refers to the sky. It was also said: to the constellations, which are the stars, which He adorned with light. The looking is by the eye. It was also said: by the heart. What it is attached to is omitted so as to be general.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَنِ استرق}: there are five aspects in it. The first: it is in the position of accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), and the meaning: "for they were not guarded against him"; more than one said it. The second: disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and its position is also accusative. The third: that it is a badal (substitute) of {كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ}, so its position is genitive; al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. There is something to consider in it, because the statement is affirmative. The fourth: that it is an adjective of {كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ}, so its position is genitive, with disagreement on this question. The fifth: that it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the clause of His saying «فأَتْبعه». The fāʾ entered only because «مَنْ» is either conditional or a relative that resembles the conditional; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, and in that case it belongs to the disconnected exception.
Al-shihāb: a flame of fire, and the star was called by it because of the intensity of its light and brilliance; its plural is shuhub in the large number, and ashhiba. Al-shuhba: whiteness mixed with blackness, by comparison with the shihāb because of its mixing with smoke; and from it is "kutayba shahbāʾ" (a grey-hued squadron) for the blackness of the men and the whiteness of the iron. From this people erred in applying al-shuhba to pure whiteness.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والأرض مَدَدْنَاهَا}: «الأرض» is accusative by preoccupation (ishtighāl), and it was not read otherwise, because it is preferable in that it is conjoined to a verbal clause before it, namely His saying {وَلَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا فِي السماء بُرُوجاً} [al-Ḥijr: 16].
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Since the clause after it is a verbal clause, the accusative was preferable to the nominative." I say: they have not counted this among the indications that favour the accusative; they counted only its being conjoined to a verbal clause before it, not the conjoining of a verbal clause to it. But it is the analogy, since a verbal clause is conjoined to its like, unlike what would be the case if you made it nominative, for then you would conjoin a verbal clause to a nominal one; yet they did not take that into account. The pronoun in «فيها» refers to the earth. It was also said: to the firm mountains. It was also said: to both.
His saying: {مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ}: «مِنْ» may be partitive, and this is the sound view, or redundant (zāʾida) according to the Kufans and al-Akhfash.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن لَّسْتُمْ}: five aspects are possible for «مَنْ». The first, which is the view of al-Zajjāj: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: «وأَعَشْنا مَنْ لستم لهم برازقين» (and We provided for those whom you do not provide for), such as slaves, beasts and wild animals. The second: that it is accusative as a conjunction to «معايش», that is: "and We made for you in it those whom you do not provide for, of the beasts from which benefit is derived." The third: that it is accusative as a conjunction to the position of «لكم». The fourth: that it is genitive as a conjunction to the «kum» which is in the genitive by the lām, and this is permitted without repeating the preposition according to the Kufans and some of the Basrans, which was verified earlier in sūrat al-Baqara at His saying {وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ والمسجد} [al-Baqara: 217]. The fifth: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, that is: «ومَنْ لستم له برازقين جَعَلْنا له فيها معايشَ» (and for those whom you do not provide for, We have made in it means of livelihood). It was heard from the Arabs: «ضربْتُ زيداً وعمروٌ», with «عمرٌو» nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is: «وعمروٌ ضربْتُه».
And «مَنْ» may be intended for rational beings, that is: "and those whom you do not provide for among your dependants, whom you claim you provide for"; and it may be intended for others, that is: "and those among the beasts whom you do not provide for, although you claim that you provide for them," and a group of the exegetes held this. It may also be intended for both kinds, and that is good in wording and meaning.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ}: «إنْ» is negative, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) on the mubtadaʾ (subject), «عندنا» is its khabar (predicate), and «خزائنُه» is its agent because it relies [on a preceding element]. It may also be that «عندنا» is the khabar of what follows it, and the clause is the khabar of the first; but the first is preferable because of the nearness of the preposition phrase to the singular.
His saying: {إِلاَّ بِقَدَرٍ}: it may be attached to the verb before it, and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, that is: "except bound up with a measure."

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَوَاقِحَ}: an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from «الرياح». Regarding «اللواقح» there are several views. The first: that it is the plural of «مُلْقِح», because it is from «أَلْقَحَ يُلْقِحُ», so it is «مُلْقِحٌ»; its proper form would be «مَلاقِح», and the mīm was omitted for lightness. It is said: «أَلْقَحتِ الريحُ السحابَ» (the wind fertilised the clouds), as it is said «ألقح الفحلُ الأنثى» (the stallion impregnated the female). Similar is «الطوائح», whose original is «المَطاوِح», because it is from «أطاح يُطيح». He [the poet] said:
293 - 7- لِيُبْكَ يزيدُ ضارعٌ لخصومةٍ ... ومُخْتَبِطٌ مِمَّا تُطيح الطَّوائِحُ (Let Yazīd be wept for by one humbled in a quarrel, and by a seeker of gifts from what the fates cast down)
This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda.
The second: that it is the plural of «لاقِح»; it is said «لَقِحَتِ الريحُ» when it carried water. Al-Azharī said: "Carriers that carry the cloud, as you say «أَلْقَحَتِ الناقةُ فَلَقِحَتْ» when she carries the foetus in her belly; the wind was likened to her, and from it is his saying:
293 - 8- إذا لَقِحَتْ حربٌ عَوانٌ مُضِرَّةٌ ... ضَروسٌ تَهِرُّ الناسَ أنيابُها عُصْلُ (when a fierce, harmful war has conceived, a biting one, whose crooked fangs snarl at the people)
The third: that it is the plural of «لاقِح» by relation, like «lābin» and «tāmir», that is: possessing fertilisation; because when the wind passes over water, then passes over the clouds and the water, there is fertilisation in it; al-Farrāʾ said it. The disagreement about «معايش» has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf, and about «يُنَزِّل», and about «الريح» in al-Baqara. Nothing remains here except for those who made «الريح» singular, for it may be asked: how is a plural ḥāl placed in the accusative from a singular? It was mentioned earlier that the generic is meant by it, and it is a plural in meaning, so there is no objection.
His saying: {فَأَسْقَيْنَاكُمُوهُ}: it is said «أَسْقاه» and «سَقاه», and their explanation will come in the sūra after it, since it was read with both. The two pronouns are joined here because they differ in rank; and if the second of them were separated it would be permissible according to others than Sībawayh, and this is as was mentioned earlier in His saying {أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا} [Hūd: 28].
His saying: {وَمَآ أَنْتُمْ لَهُ بِخَازِنِينَ}: a resumptive clause, and «له» is attached to «خازنين».

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لَنَحْنُ}: «نحن» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «نُحْيِيْ» its khabar (predicate), and the clause the khabar of «إنَّا». It may also be an emphasis (tawkīd) of the «nā» in «إنَّا». It may not be a separator (faṣl) because it does not fall between two nouns, and its parallel was mentioned earlier. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not a separator for two reasons. One: a verb follows it. The second: the lām accompanies it." I say: the second reason is a mistake, for the lām of emphasis is not prevented from entering on the separator; the grammarians stated this explicitly, and from it is His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ القصص} [Āl ʿImrān: 62], where they allowed the separator even though it is accompanied by the lām.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن صَلْصَالٍ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent or for partition. Al-ṣalṣāl: Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is the clay mixed with sand, which then dries, so a ringing is heard from it, that is, a sound." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The dry clay that rings without being baked; when it is baked it is pottery (fakhkhār)." Abū l-Haytham said: "It is the sound of a bridle and the like, such as the rattling in a garment." Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "They said: if you imagine in its sound a prolongation, it is ṣalīl; and if you imagine in it a repetition, it is ṣalṣala. It was also said: it is from the doubling of «ṣill», when it stank." End [of the quotation]. And ṣalṣāl here is in the sense of muṣalṣil, like zalzāl in the sense of muzalzil; and the pattern faʿlāl may also be a maṣdar, like al-zilzāl. Kasra on it is also permissible.
Regarding the pattern of this kind, I mean what has its first and second radicals repeated, there is disagreement. It was said: its pattern is faʿfaʿ, the fāʾ and ʿayn being repeated and the word having no lām; al-Farrāʾ and others said it. This is a mistake, because the minimum of roots is three: fāʾ, ʿayn and lām. The second: that its pattern is faʿfal, and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. The third: that it is faʿʿal with doubled ʿayn, its original being ṣallal; when three like letters came together, the second was substituted by a letter of the same kind as the first radical of the word, and this is a Kufan position. Some restricted this disagreement to cases where the meaning is not impaired by its dropping, such as lamlama and kabkaba, for you say of them lamma and kabba; but if the meaning would not remain sound with its dropping, such as simsim, he said, there is no disagreement about the originality of all [the letters].
His saying: {مِّنْ حَمَإٍ}: there are two aspects in it. One: that it is in the position of genitive as an adjective of ṣalṣāl, attached to an omitted element. The second: that it is a badal (substitute) of «صَلْصال» with the preposition repeated.
Al-ḥamaʾ: black, stinking mud. Al-Layth said: "its singular is ḥamaʾa, with a vowel on the ʿayn," making it a generic noun; but he made a mistake in that, for the language scholars said it is said only «ḥamʾa» with sukūn, and the vowelled form is not known, as Abū ʿUbayda and a group stated explicitly, and they recited the verse of Abū l-Aswad:
293 - 9- يجيءُ بِمِلْئِها طَوْراً وطَوْراً ... يَجِيءُ بِحَمْأَةٍ وقليلِ ماءِ (At times it comes with its fill, and at times it comes with mud and a little water)
So «al-ḥamʾa» is not the singular of «al-ḥamaʾ», because of the difference of the two patterns.
Al-masnūn: poured out, from their saying «سَنَنْتُ الشرابَ», as though, because of its moistness, it was made poured like other liquids; so the meaning is as if: he poured out the form of a human being as molten jewels are poured. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Masnūn in the sense of «muṣawwar» (formed) should properly be an adjective of ṣalṣāl, as though He poured out the mud and formed from it the figure of a person." I say: he means that the implied form becomes «مِنْ صَلْصالٍِ مُصَوَّر»; but this requires putting the interpreted description before the explicit one, if we make {مِّنْ حَمَإٍ} an adjective of ṣalṣāl, whereas if we make it a badal, it does not. It was also said: masnūn is formed, from sunnat al-wajh, which is its form. The poet said:
294 - 0- تُريكَ سُنَّة وَجْهٍ غيرَ مُقْرِفَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (She shows you the form of a face, not of low birth ...)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From «سَنَنْتُ الحجرَ بالحجر» when you rub it with it, and what flows between them is «sanīn», and it is always stinking." It was also said: al-masnūn is the one ascribed to him [Ādam], the meaning being that offspring are ascribed to him, and this speaker seems to have taken it from what occurs. It was also said: it is from «أسِن الماءُ» when it changed, and this is a mistake because of the difference of the two roots.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والجآن خَلَقْنَاهُ}: accusative by preoccupation (ishtighāl), and its accusative is preferred because its clause is conjoined to a verbal clause. Al-jānn, or al-jinn, is Iblīs, as Ādam is the father of humankind. It was also said: a name for the genus of the jinn.
Al-Ḥasan read «والجَأَنَّ», and the discussion of that was given near the end of al-Fātiḥa.
{مِن قَبْلُ} and {مِن نَّارِ} are both attached to «خَلَقْنا», because the first is for the beginning of the extent and the second is for partition. In it is evidence that «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent in time, and the Basrans' interpretation of it and its parallels is far-fetched.
Al-samūm: what kills by excess of heat, whether of sun, wind or fire, because it enters the pores and kills. It was also said: al-samūm is what occurs at night, and al-ḥarūr what occurs in the day.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَجْمَعُونَ}: a second emphasis (tawkīd), and it does not denote togetherness in time, contrary to some. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It would be a ḥāl, [not] an emphasis," meaning that it conveys the benefit of a ḥāl while being an emphasis; and there is something to consider in it, since there is no contradiction between the two in terms of meaning. Do you not see that «جاؤوني جميعاً» is permissible while it conveys emphasis? Your verification of this was given earlier, along with the anecdote of Thaʿlab and Ibn Qādim.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لأَسْجُدَ}: this is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd).
And His saying: {فَقَعُواْ لَهُ} [al-Ḥijr: 29]: the lām may be attached to the verb before it, and may be attached to «ساجدين». Parallels of the words of this story were given earlier in al-Baqara and al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إلى يَوْمِ}: it may be attached to the settledness (istiqrār) in «عليك», and it may be attached to the curse itself.

semin-durr:39-39.t: And the pronoun in {لَهُمْ} refers to the descendants of Ādam, even though no mention of them has preceded, because they are known.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هَذَا صِرَاطٌ}: «هذا» is a pointer to sincerity (ikhlāṣ), understood from «المُخْلَصين». It was also said: «هذا» means the negation of his [Iblīs's] adorning and misleading. And «عليَّ» means: whoever passes over it passes over Me, that is, over My good pleasure and My honour. It was also said: «على» is in the sense of «إلى», reported from al-Ḥasan.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abū Rajāʾ, Ibn Sīrīn and Yaʿqūb, among others, read: «عَلِيٌّ», that is: high and exalted.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَنِ اتبعك مِنَ الغاوين}: there are two aspects in it. One: that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), because what is meant by «عبادي» is the generality, the obedient among them and the disobedient. In that case it follows that the greater part is excepted from the lesser, and that is a question of disagreement.
The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because the misguided are not included in «عبادي», since what is meant by it are the sincere, and the annexation is an annexation of honour.

semin-durr:43-43.t: And {أَجْمَعِينَ}: an emphasis (tawkīd). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "An emphasis with the meaning of a ḥāl (circumstantial)," and in it is an inclination toward those who hold the unity of time. His saying: {لَمَوْعِدُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ}: regarding «أجمعين» there are two aspects, the more apparent being that it is an emphasis of the pronoun. The second: that it is a ḥāl from it, and the operator in it is the meaning of annexation; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. You have learned the disagreement of people about a ḥāl coming from the muḍāf ilayhi (the annexed-to term). Al-mawʿid cannot govern it if place is meant by it; if the maṣdar is meant, it may govern since it is a maṣdar, but an annexed term must be omitted, that is: «مكان موعدِهم» (the place of their appointment).

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ}: this clause may be resumptive, and that is the apparent view; it may also be a second khabar (predicate). It may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جهنم» because «inna» does not govern a ḥāl; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. By analogy with what they mentioned regarding «layta», «ka-anna» and «laʿalla» among its sisters, namely that they govern a ḥāl because they are in the sense of «I wished», «I compared» and «I hoped», «inna» should also govern in it, because it is in the sense of «I affirmed»; for this reason it acted as the verb acts, and it is the root of the chapter.
His saying «منهم»: it may be a ḥāl from «جُزْء», because in origin it is an adjective of it, and when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl. It may also be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition phrase, which is «لكلِّ بابٍ», and the operator in this ḥāl is what operates in this preposition phrase. It cannot be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «مَقْسُوم» because an adjective does not govern what precedes the thing described. It cannot be an adjective of «باب» because the door is not from the people.
Abū Jaʿfar read with doubled zāy without hamza, as though he shifted the vowel of the hamza onto the zāy, and paused on it, doubling it, as in their saying «خالدّْ»; then he treated connected reading like pausing.

semin-durr:45-45.t: Ibn Kathīr, the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Abū Bakr and Ibn Dhakwān put kasra on the ʿayn of {وَعُيُونٍ} when indefinite, and of «العِيون» when definite, wherever it occurs. The rest read with ḍamma, which is the original.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ادخلوها}: the majority read it with the hamza of connection, from «دَخَل يَدْخُل». The disagreement of the readers over the vowel of this tanwīn, because of the meeting of two sākin letters, was mentioned in al-Baqara. Yaʿqūb read with fatḥa on the tanwīn and kasra on the khāʾ. Its explanation: it is an imperative of «أَدْخَل يُدْخِل»; when it fell after «عيون», he shifted the vowel of the hamza onto the tanwīn because it is a hamza of severance (qaṭʿ), then omitted it. The command is from Allah the Exalted to the angels, that is: «أَدْخِلوها إياهم» (cause them to enter it).
Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb also read «أُدْخِلوها» as a past passive, except that Yaʿqūb put ḍamma on the tanwīn. Its explanation: he took it from the quadriliteral «أَدْخَلَ», and shifted the vowel of the hamza of severance onto the tanwīn, as he shifted the fatḥa in his first reading. Al-Ḥasan put kasra on it according to the principle of the meeting of two sākin letters; its explanation: he treated the hamza of severance as the hamza of connection in dropping.
The imperative reading is on an implied saying, that is: "It will be said to the people of Paradise: ادْخُلوها," or "It will be said to the angels: أَدْخِلُوها إياهم." On the reading as a report, it is resumptive, without an implied saying.
His saying «بسلامٍ»: a ḥāl, that is: "bound up with safety," or "being greeted with peace."
His saying «آمِنين»: another ḥāl, which is a badal (substitute) of what precedes it: either a total substitute (badal kull min kull) or a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because security includes greeting, or the reverse.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِخْوَاناً}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «هم» in «صدورِهم», and this is permitted because the muḍāf (annexed term) is a part of the muḍāf ilayhi. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The operator in it is the meaning of adhesion." It may also be a ḥāl from the agent of «ادْخُلوها», as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara); so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, but there is no need for it; rather it is a concurrent ḥāl. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «آمِنين», and a ḥāl from the pronoun in His saying {فِي جَنَّاتٍ}.
His saying: {على سُرُرٍ}: it may be attached to «إخواناً» itself, because it is in the sense of "being sincere to one another on couches"; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, and there is something to consider in it, in that it interprets a rigid noun by a derived one, which is far from it. On this «متقابلين» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إخواناً». It may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «إخوان», and on this «متقابلين» is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition phrase. It may be attached to «متقابلين», that is: "facing one another on couches," and on this «متقابلين» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إخواناً» or an adjective of «إخواناً». It may also be accusative in praise (naṣb ʿalā l-madḥ), meaning that it cannot be an adjective of the pronoun, so it was cut off.
Al-surur: the plural of sarīr, which is well known. In «سُرُر» and the like, of what is pluralised on this pattern from the doubled faʿīl, fatḥa on the ʿayn is permitted for lightness; this is the dialect of Kalb and Tamīm, who say «سُرَرٌ» and «ذُلَلٌ» in the plural of «سَرير» and «ذَليل».

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌ}: this may be resumptive, and may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «متقابلين». Al-naṣab: fatigue. It is said from it: «نَصِبَ يَنْصِبُ» so he is «نَصِبٌ» and «ناصِب», and «أَنْصَبَني كذا» (such a thing wearied me). He [the poet] said:
294 - 1- تأوَّبَني هَمٌّ مع الليلِ مُنْصِبُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (A wearying anxiety visited me with the night ...)
and «همٌّ ناصِبٌ» means: possessing fatigue, like «lābin» and «tāmir». Al-Nābigha said:
294 - 2- كِلِيْني لِهَمٍّ يا أُميمةُ ناصِبِ ... وليلٍ أقاسيه بَطِيْءِ الكواكبِ (Leave me to an anxiety, O Umayma, that wearies, and a night I endure, slow in its stars)
And «منها» is attached to «مُخْرَجِيْن».

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَا الغفور}: «أنا» may be an emphasis (tawkīd), a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a separator (faṣl).

semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying, the Exalted: {هُوَ العذاب}: «هو» may be a mubtadaʾ or a separator (faṣl); emphasis is not permissible, since an overt noun is not emphasised by a pronoun.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ دَخَلُواْ}: regarding «إذ» there are two aspects. One: that it is an object of an implied verb, that is: «اذكر إذ دخلوا» (remember when they entered). The second: that it is an adverbial (ẓarf) in its usual function. Regarding what governs it there are two aspects. One: that it is omitted, its implied form being the khabar (predicate) of «ضيفِ». The second: that it is «ضيف» itself. In justifying that there are two aspects. One: that since it was originally a maṣdar, that is taken into account in it; and what indicates that its maṣdar nature is taken into account, even after its use as a description, is its lack of agreement with what precedes it in dual, plural and feminine, for the most part, and the fact that it stands in the place of a description, and a description governs. The second: that it is on the omission of an annexed term, that is: «أصحاب ضيفِ إبراهيم», that is, his hospitality; so the maṣdar remains in its state, and for that reason it governs.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said, after implying «أصحاب ضيافته» (the people of his hospitality): "On this the maṣdar is annexed to the object." I say: there is something to consider in it, since the apparent view is that it is annexed to its agent, since the Prophet ﷺ is . . . . . . . .
[Translator's note: the entry ends in the source with a row of dots after «هو»; the sentence is incomplete in the source and I have not completed it.]

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَوْجَلْ}: the majority read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, from «وَجِل» like «شَرِب يَشْرَب»; fatḥa is the analogical form of faʿila, except that the Arabs preferred yafʿil with kasra in some words when the first radical is a wāw, as in «يَثِقُ».
Al-Ḥasan read «تُوْجَل» as a passive from «الإِيجال». And «لا تَاجَل» was read; the original is «تَوْجَل» like the reading of the majority, except that he substituted an alif for the wāw because of the fatḥa before it, even though it is not vowelled, as in their saying «تابة» and «صامة» for «تَوْبة» and «صَوْمَة»; and it was heard: "O Allah, accept my tāba and my ṣāma." It was also read «لا تَوَاجَلْ», from «المواجلة».

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَبَشَّرْتُمُونِي}: al-Aʿraj read «بَشَّرْتموني» without the interrogative particle, so it admits a statement and admits a question; he omitted the particle only because it is known.
His saying: {على أَن مَّسَّنِيَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Ibn Muḥayṣin read «الكُبْرُ» on the pattern of qufl.
His saying: {فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ}: «بِمَ» is attached to «تُبَشِّرون», and it is put first necessarily because it has the head of the sentence. The majority read with fatḥa on the nūn, lightened, as the nūn of the nominative, and the object of the glad tidings is not mentioned. Nāfiʿ read it with kasra; the original is «تُبَشِّرُوني», and he omitted the yāʾ, content with the kasra in its place. Abū Ḥātim declared this mistaken and said: "This occurs in poetry by necessity."
Makkī said: "Some people have criticised this reading because of its remoteness in Arabic, because omitting the nūn that accompanies the yāʾ is not good except in poetry; and if the first nūn is taken to be omitted, you have dropped the sign of the nominative without any accusative or jussive operator; and because kasra on the nūn of the nominative is ugly, for its due is fatḥa." This criticism is not to be heeded, because the first-person yāʾ is very often omitted with kasra sufficing in its place, and it has been read thus in His saying {أَفَغَيْرَ الله تأمروني} [al-Zumar: 64], as its explanation will come.
Its explanation: when two nūns came together, one for the nominative and the other the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), the wording was felt heavy: some assimilated, and some omitted. Then there was disagreement about the omitted one: is it the first or the second? I have given the proofs of each view fully in sūrat al-Anʿām. Ibn Kathīr read it with doubling, with kasra, assimilating the first into the second and omitting the yāʾ of the first person. Al-Ḥasan retained the yāʾ together with doubling the nūn. What favours the reading of the one who retained the object of «تُبَشِّرون», which is the yāʾ, is His saying: {قَالُواْ بَشَّرْنَاكَ}.

semin-durr:55-55.t: And {بالحق}: attached to the verb before it, and it is weak for it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "We gave you glad tidings while the truth is with us."

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن يَقْنَطُ}: the meaning of this question is negation; for this reason affirmation follows it with «إلا». Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «يَقْنِط» with kasra on the ʿayn of this imperfect wherever it occurs, and the rest with fatḥa; Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Ashhab with ḍamma. In the past there are two dialects: «قَنِط» with kasra on the nūn, with «يَقْنَطُ» with fatḥa; and «قَنَط» with fatḥa, with «يَقْنِط» with kasra. Were it not that reading is a followed practice (sunna), the analogy for the one who read «يَقْنَطُ» with fatḥa would be to read its past as «قَنِط» with kasra; but they agreed on fatḥa in His saying {مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ} [al-Shūrā: 28]. Fatḥa in the past is the more frequent, and for that reason there is agreement on it. What favours the reading «يَقْنَطُ» with fatḥa is the reading of Abū ʿAmr in some transmissions {فَلاَ تَكُن مِّنَ القانطين}, like «فَرِح يَفْرَحُ فهو فَرِح». Al-qunūṭ: extreme despair of good.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ آلَ لُوطٍ}: [there are aspects] in it. The first: that it is a connected exception (mustathnā muttaṣil), excepted from the latent pronoun in «مجرمين», meaning: "all of them were criminals except the family of Lūṭ, for they were not criminals," and His saying {إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ} would be a resumptive report of their deliverance since they were not criminals; the sending would then include the criminals and the family of Lūṭ, for the destruction of the former and the deliverance of the latter.
The second: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because the family of Lūṭ were not included at all among the criminals. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "When it is a disconnected exception, it is one in which the accusative is obligatory, because it is among exceptions in which the governing element cannot be directed to the excepted; for they were not sent to them, but were sent only to the criminal people specifically. His saying {إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ} would run in the course of the khabar of «لكن» in its connection with the family of Lūṭ, since the meaning is: 'but the family of Lūṭ are those whom We shall deliver.' Some grammarians claimed, in a disconnected exception implied by «لكن», when nothing follows it that can be a predicate, that the predicate is omitted and that it is in the position of nominative because of the application of «illā» and its implication by «lākin»."
I say: there is something to consider in it, because their saying that the governing element cannot be directed to it means that it is not possible, as in «ضحك القومُ إلا حمارَهم» ("the people laughed except their donkey") and «صَهِلَت الخيلُ إلا الإبلَ» ("the horses neighed except the camels"). As for this, sending to them would be possible without prevention. As for his saying "because they were not sent to them," it is correct, because the rule of exception in all cases is thus, namely that it be excluded from what the first was judged by; but if the governing element were directed to it, that would be sound, unlike the examples of theirs I mentioned.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ امرأته}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is an exception from the family of Lūṭ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "When an exception comes after an exception, the second exception is related to the mubtadaʾ (subject), as in your saying «له عندي عشرةٌ إلا أربعةً إلا درهماً» ('he has ten with me except four except a dirham'); for the dirham is excepted from the four, so it is added to the ten, as though you had said: eleven except four, or ten except three."
The second: that it is excepted from the genitive pronoun in «مُنجُّوهم». Al-Zamakhsharī forbade the first aspect and specified the second, saying: "If you say: from what is «إلا امرأته» excepted? Is it an exception from an exception? I say: it is excepted from the genitive pronoun in His saying «لمنجُّوهُمْ», and it is not at all an exception from an exception; for an exception from an exception occurs only where the ruling is the same, and it is said: «We destroyed them except the family of Lūṭ except his wife», as it is the same in the saying of the one who pronounces divorce: «You are divorced three times except two except one», and the saying of one who acknowledges a debt to someone: «I owe ten except three except a dirham». As for the verse, the two rulings differ, because {إِلاَّ آلَ لُوطٍ} is attached to «أَرْسَلْنا» or to «مجرمين», whereas {إِلاَّ امرأته} is attached to His saying «لمنجُّوهم»; so how could it be an exception from an exception?"
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Since al-Zamakhsharī had assumed that «امرأته» is an exception from the pronoun in «لمنجُّوهم», how can it be an exception from an exception? As for the one who said that it is an exception from an exception, his statement can be made sound in one of two ways. One: that since «امرأتَه» is excepted from the pronoun in «لمنجُّوهم», which refers back to the family of Lūṭ, it is as though it were excepted from the family of Lūṭ, because the pronoun is the overt noun. The other aspect: that His saying {إِلاَّ آلَ لُوطٍ}, since He ruled on them with a ruling other than that with which He ruled on a criminal people, required their deliverance, so His saying {إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ} came as an emphasis of the meaning of the exception, the meaning being: except the family of Lūṭ, to whom no punishment was sent, and their deliverance follows from the absence of sending punishment to them. So it became parallel to your saying «قام القومُ إلا زيداً لم يَقُمْ» or «إلا زيداً فإنه لم يَقُمْ»; this clause is an emphasis of what the exception includes of ruling on what follows «illā» the opposite of the ruling preceding on the excepted-from. So «إلا امرأته», on this explanation we have given, is excepted from the family of Lūṭ, because an exception from what is brought to establish is preferable to an exception from what is brought for emphasis."
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «لمُنَجُوْهم» lightened, and they likewise lightened the verb of this description in His saying, the Exalted, in al-ʿAnkabūt: {لَنُنَجِّيَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ} [verse 32], and likewise they lightened His saying in it: {إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ} [verse 33]; so the two run on one course.
Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr agreed with them on lightening «مُنْجوك», as though they combined the two dialects. The rest of the Seven read all of them doubled. Lightening and doubling are two well-known dialects, from «نَجَّى» and «أَنْجَى» like «أَنْزَلَ» and «نَزَّل», and the verbs of both have been used: He said {فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 65] and in another place {أَنجَاهُمْ} [Yūnus: 23].
His saying «قَدَّرْناها»: Abū Bakr read with the dāl lightened and the rest with it doubled; they are two dialects, «قَدَرَ» and «قدَّر», and this disagreement also runs in sūrat al-Naml.
His saying «إنَّها»: kasra was put on it because of the lām in its predicate, and it is a suspending one (muʿallaqa) of what precedes it, because the verb of estimation is suspended, treated like the verb of knowing: either because it is in its sense, or because it follows from it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is suspension of the verb of estimation permitted in «قَدَّرْنَآ إِنَّهَا», when suspension is among the properties of verbs of the heart? I say: because the verb of estimation includes the meaning of knowing." The Shaykh said: "«إنها» was given kasra by treating the verb of estimation like the verb of knowing." I say: this is not valid as a reason for its kasra; it suits only as a reason for its suspending the verb before it. The reason for its kasra is what I mentioned before, namely the presence of the lām, and without it fatḥa would have been put.

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying, the Exalted: {بَلْ جِئْنَاكَ}: a turning away (iḍrāb) from an omitted object, its implied form being: "We did not come to you with what is denied; rather, We came to you [with ...]."

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The disagreement over His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَسْرِ}, with severance and connection of the hamza, has been mentioned in Hūd. The Yemeni read, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya and the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» reported, «فَسِرْ», from «al-sayr». A group read «بقِطَع» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ. It was mentioned in Yūnus that al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Kathīr read it with sukūn in His saying «قطعاً», and the rest with fatḥa.
His saying: {حَيْثُ تُؤْمَرُونَ}: «حيث» is in its usual function as an adverb of vague place, and because of its vagueness the verb is transitive to it without an intermediary, although in poetry there has come transitivity to it by «في», as in his saying:
294 - 3- فَأصْبَحَ في حيثُ التقَيْنا شريدُهُمْ ... طَليقٌ ومكتوفُ اليدين ومُزْعِفُ (So their fugitive, at the place where we met, was free, or bound at the hands, or struck down)
Some of them claimed that here it is an adverb of time, inferring from His saying «بقِطْعٍ من الليل», then He said {وامضوا حَيْثُ تُؤْمَرُونَ}, that is: at that time. This is weak, and had it been as he said, the construction would have been «حيث أُمِرْتم»; and even if the construction had come so, there would be no proof in it.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ}: He included in «قضاء» the meaning of revelation (īḥāʾ), so it was made transitive by «إلى»; similar is {وَقَضَيْنَآ إلى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ} [al-Isrāʾ: 4].
His saying: {ذَلِكَ الأمر}: «ذلك» is the object of the decree, and the pointer is to what He promised of the destruction of his people; and «الأمرَ» is either a badal (substitute) of it or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it.
His saying: {أَنَّ دَابِرَ}: the majority read «أنَّ» with fatḥa, and there are several aspects in it. The first: that it is a badal of «ذلك», if we say «الأمر» is an explicative apposition. The second: that it is a badal of «الأمر», whether we say it is an explicative apposition or a badal of what precedes it. The third: that it is on the omission of the preposition, that is: «بأنَّ دابِرَ», so it has the well-known disagreement.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with kasra, because it is in the sense of saying, or on an implied saying. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] gave the reason that, since what is in the sense of knowing is suspended, kasra was put. And in it is the consideration mentioned earlier.
His saying: {مُّصْبِحِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «مقطوعٌ»; it is plural only by construing according to the meaning. Al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd made it the predicate of an implied «kāna», saying: "its implied form is «إذا كانوا مُصْبِحين», like «أنتَ ماشياً أحسنُ منك راكباً»." That is a strain. And «مُصْبِحين» means entering the morning, so «kāna» is complete.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: and {يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هَؤُلآءِ بَنَاتِي}: several aspects are possible in it. The first: that «بناتي» is the object of an implied verb, that is: «تَزَوَّجوا هؤلاء» (marry these); and «بناتي» is an explication or a badal. The second: that «هؤلاء بناتي» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar (subject and predicate), and something omitted is needed to complete the benefit, that is: «فَتَزَوَّجُوْهن» (so marry them). The third: that «هؤلاء» is a mubtadaʾ and «بناتي» a badal or explication, and the khabar is omitted, that is: «هُنَّ أطهرُ لكم» (they are purer for you), as it came in the parallel [verse].
His saying: {فَلاَ تَفْضَحُونِ} [al-Ḥijr: 68]: al-faḍḥ and al-faḍīḥa are making plain and manifest, and from it comes «فَضَحَه الصُّبْحُ» (the dawn exposed him). He [the poet] said:
294 - 4- ولاحَ ضوءُ هِلالِ الليل يَفْضَحُنا ... مثلَ القُلامَةِ قد قُصَّتْ من الظُفُرِ (The light of the night's crescent appeared, exposing us, like a nail-paring that has been cut off)
except that al-faḍīḥa is specific to what is a disgrace to a person when it comes to light.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَعَمْرُكَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is necessarily omitted; similar is «لايْمُنُ الله». And «إنهم» and what falls within its scope is the answer to the oath, its implied form being: «لَعَمْرك قسمي أو يميني إنهم» (By your life is my oath: they ...). Al-ʿamr and al-ʿumr, with fatḥa and ḍamma, mean continuance, except that they adhered to fatḥa in the oath. Al-Zajjāj said: "Because it is lighter for them, and they swear frequently by «لَعَمْري» and «لَعَمْرك»." It has many rules, among them: whenever it is accompanied by the lām of inchoation (lām al-ibtidāʾ), nominative as mubtadaʾ is obligatory in it and its khabar is omitted, the answer to the oath standing in its place. Among them: that it becomes explicit in oath, that is, specified in it, unlike other expressions such as «عهدُ الله وميثاقُه». Among them: that fatḥa on its ʿayn is obligatory; and if the lām of inchoation does not accompany it, accusative by an implied verb is permitted, as in «عَمْرَ اللهِ لأفعلنَّ»; and in that case two aspects are allowed in the Majestic Name: accusative and nominative. The accusative is on its being a maṣdar annexed to its agent, and in that there are two meanings. One: the original is «أسألُكَ بتعميرك اللهَ» (I ask you by your attributing everlastingness to Allah), that is, by your describing Allah the Exalted as everlasting, then the additions of the maṣdar were omitted. The second: the meaning is "your worship of Allah," for al-ʿamr is worship; Ibn al-Aʿrābī related «عَمَرْتُ ربي», that is, I worshipped Him, and «فلانٌ عامِرٌ ربِّه», that is, his worshipper.
As for the nominative: it is on its being annexed to its object. Al-Fārisī said: "Its meaning is «عَمَّرَك اللهُ تَعْميراً» (may Allah grant you long life)." Al-Akhfash said: "Its original is «أسألك بتعميرك اللهَ», and the additions of the maṣdar, the verb and the bāʾ were omitted, so it became accusative; it is also permissible to mention its khabar, so you say «عَمْرُك قَسَمي لأقومَنَّ»; and ḍamma on its ʿayn is also permissible." The saying of the poet is recited in both ways:
294 - 5- أيُّها المُنْكِحُ الثُّرَيَّا سُهَيْلاً ... عَمْرَكَ اللهَ كيفَ يلتقيانِ (O you who marry al-Thurayyā to Suhayl, by your life, by Allah, how can they meet?)
The genitive bāʾ may also enter it, as in «بعَمْرِكَ لأفعلَنَّ». He said:
294 - 6- رُقَيَّ بعَمْرِكُمْ لا تَهْجُرِينا ... ومَنَّيْنا المُنَى ثم امْطُلِينا (Ruqayya, by your life, do not forsake us; promise us wishes, then delay us)
It is one of the nouns that necessarily take annexation, so it is not cut off from it, and it is annexed to everything. Some claimed that it is not annexed to Allah. It was said: perhaps the one who said this imagined that it is used only for disconnection; yet its annexation to the Creator, the Exalted, has been heard. The poet said:
294 - 7- إذا رَضِيَتْ عليَّ بنو قُشَيْرٍ ... لعَمْرُ اللهِ أَعْجبني رِضاها (When the Banū Qushayr are pleased with me, by the life of Allah, their pleasure delights me)
Some forbade its annexation to the first-person yāʾ, saying: because it is an oath by the life of the one who swears; but this has occurred. Al-Nābigha said:
294 - 3- لَعَمْري -وما عَمْري عليَّ بهَيِّنٍ- ... لقد نَطَقَتْ بُطْلاً عَلَيَّ الأقارِعُ (By my life — and my life is not light to me — the Aqāriʿ have spoken falsehood against me)
[Translator's note: the verse number appears as 294 - 3 in the source, repeating the number used earlier in this book for another verse; I have kept it as written.]
The Arabs have inverted it by putting its rāʾ before its lām, saying «رَعَمْلي», and it is poor.
The majority read «إنَّ» with kasra because the lām falls in its predicate. Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of al-Jahḍamī, read it with fatḥa. Its analysis is on the redundancy of the lām, and it is like the reading of Ibn Jubayr: {إِلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطعام} [al-Furqān: 20], with fatḥa.
And al-Aʿmash [read] «سَكْرِهم» without a tāʾ; Ibn Abī ʿAbla [read] «سَكَراتهم» as a plural; and al-Ashhab [read] «سُكْرَتِهم» with ḍamma on the sīn.
And «يَعْمَهُون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the preposition phrase, or from the pronoun that is genitive by annexation. The operator is either «سَكْرَة» itself, since it is a maṣdar, or the meaning of the annexation.

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مُشْرِقِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «أَخَذَتْهم», that is: entering the sunrise.

semin-durr:74-74.t: And the pronoun in {عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا} refers to the city. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "to the towns of the people of Lūṭ." The first was preferred because something has preceded to which it can refer in wording, unlike the second.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ}: attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «آيات». The better view is that it is attached to «آياتٍ» itself, because it is in the sense of signs. Al-tawassum is a tafaʿʿul form from al-wasm. Al-wasm: its original meaning is steadfastness and reflection, taken from al-wasm, which is the marking with an iron on the skin of a camel or other animal. Thaʿlab said: "The wāsim is the one who looks at you from your head to your foot," and in it is the meaning of steadfastness. It was also said: its original is the thorough pursuit of recognition; it is said «تَوَسَّمْتُ», that is, I recognised, pursuing the ways of recognition thoroughly. He said:
294 - 9- أوَ كلما وَرَدَتْ عُكاظَ قبيلةٌ ... بَعَثَتْ إليَّ عريفَها يتوسَّمُ (Whenever a tribe came to ʿUkāẓ, did it send its chief to me to scrutinize?)
It was also said: it is a tafaʿʿul from al-wasm, which is the mark: «تَوَسَّمْتُ فيك خيراً», that is, its brand appeared to him upon you. Ibn Rawāḥa said of the Prophet ﷺ:
295 - 0- إنِّي تَوَسَّمْتُ فيك الخيرَ أَعْرِفُه ... والله يَعلم أني ثابتُ البَصَرِ (I discerned goodness in you, which I recognise, and Allah knows that I am steady of sight)
and another said:
295 - 1- تَوَسَّمْتُه لَمَّا رَأَيْتُ مَهابَةً ... عليهِ وقُلْتُ: المرءُ مِنْ آلِ هاشمِ (I scrutinized him when I saw awe upon him, and said: the man is of the House of Hāshim)
It is said «اتَّسَمَ الرجلُ» when he adopted a mark for himself by which he is known, and «تَوَسَّمَ» when he sought the pasture of al-wasmī, that is, the herbage that grows at the first rain of [spring].

semin-durr:76-76.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّهَا لَبِسَبِيلٍ}: the apparent view is that the pronoun refers to the city or the towns. It was also said: to the stones. It was also said: to the signs.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن كَانَ أَصْحَابُ}: «إنْ» is the lightened one and the lām is the distinguishing lām (fāriqa); its rule was mentioned earlier. Al-aykah: the entangled tree, singular of al-ayk. He said:
295 - 2- تَجْلُوْ بقادِمَتَيْ حَمامةِ أيْكةٍ ... بَرَداً أُسِفَّ لِثاتُه بالإثْمِدِ (She polishes with the fore-feathers of a dove of the thicket hailstones, whose gums have been dusted with kohl)
It is also said «لَيْكَة». The explanation of this will come, God willing, where the readers differ on it, in al-Shuʿarāʾ.

semin-durr:79-79.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّهُمَا لَبِإِمَامٍ}: regarding the dual pronoun there are several views. The most preferred: that it refers to the two towns, of the people of Lūṭ and the dwellers of the Thicket, who are the people of Shuʿayb, because they were mentioned earlier. It was also said: it refers to Lūṭ and Shuʿayb; yet Shuʿayb has not been mentioned, but the mention of his people indicates him. It was also said: it refers to the two reports: the report of the destruction of the people of Lūṭ and the report of the destruction of the people of Shuʿayb. It was also said: it refers to the dwellers of the Thicket and the dwellers of Madyan, because he was sent to both, so the mention of one of them implies the other.

semin-durr:83-83.t: And {مُصْبِحِينَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) as was mentioned earlier, and [the verb] is complete.

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فَمَآ أغنى}: it may be negative, or interrogative with the sense of exclamation. And «ما» may be maṣdar-forming, that is, "their earning," or an indefinite noun with a description, or in the sense of «alladhī», with the returning pronoun omitted, that is: "a thing they earn," or "that which they earn."

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ بالحق}: an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "a creation bound up with the truth."

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا}: there are several views in it. One: that the kāf is attached to «آتيناك», which al-Zamakhsharī held, for he said: "that is: We sent down upon you the like of what We sent down upon the People of the Book, and they are the divisors (al-muqtasimūn) who made the Qurʾān into parts (ʿiḍīn)." The second: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, accusative by «آتيناك», its implied form being: «آتَيْناك إتْياناً كما أَنْزَلْنا» (We gave you a giving as We sent down). The third: that it is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, but one which meets «آتيناك» in meaning, not in wording, its implied form being: «أَنْزَلْنا إليك إنزالاً كما أَنْزَلْنا», because «آتيناك» is in the sense of «أَنْزَلْنَا إليك». The fourth: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar whose operator is also implied, its implied form being: «مَتَّعْناهم تمتيعاً كما أَنْزَلْنا» (We gave them enjoyment as We sent down), and the meaning: We gave comfort to some of them as We punished others. The fifth: that it is an attribute of a maṣdar indicated by «النذير», and the implied form: «أنا النذيرُ إنْذاراً كما أَنْزَلْنا», that is, like what We sent down.
The sixth: that it is an adjective of an omitted object, whose accusative operator is «النذير», its implied form being: «النذير عذاباً، كما أنزلنا على المُقْتَسِمين» (the warner of a punishment, like that which We sent down upon the divisors), who are the people of Ṣāliḥ, because they said: {لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ} [al-Naml: 49] and swore (aqsamū) to that; or by them Quraysh is meant, since they divided (qasamū) the Qurʾān into sorcery, poetry and fabrication. Some of them rejected this on the ground that it requires an adjective to govern while described, which is not permissible according to the Basrans but is permissible according to the Kufans; had it governed and then been described, it would be permissible according to all.
The seventh: that it is an object, whose accusative operator is also «النذير». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The second: that it is attached to His saying «وقل: إني أنا النذيرُ المبين», that is: warn Quraysh of the like of the punishment We sent down upon the divisors, meaning the Jews, which is what befell Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr." This is rejected by the above objection of an adjective governing while described.
The eighth: that it is accusative as an adjective of an implied object, the accusative operator of that omitted element being implied, as the wording of «النذير» indicates it, that is: «أُنْذِرُكم عذاباً مثلَ العذابِ المنزَّلِ على المقتسمين», who are the people of Ṣāliḥ or Quraysh; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, as though he were fleeing from its being accusative by the wording of «النذير», because of the Basran objection mentioned.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya objected to the sixth view, saying: "The kāf in His saying «كما» is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: «وقل إني أنا النذيرُ المبينُ عذاباً كما أنزَلْنا»; so the kāf is a noun in the position of accusative. This is the statement of the exegetes. In my view it is not sound, because {كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا} is not among what Muḥammad, peace be upon him, says, but is of the words of Allah the Exalted, so the speech is cut off; this view is arranged only if Allah the Exalted said to him: «Warn of a punishment as ...». What I say about this is: the meaning is: «And say: I am the plain warner, as our messengers said before you, and We sent down upon them as We sent down upon you». It is also possible that the meaning is: «And say: I am the plain warner, as We have sent down in the Books that you would come as a warner», on the basis that the divisors are the People of the Book." End [of the quotation].
Some excused what Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] said, saying: "The kāf is attached to an omitted element which the meaning indicates, its implied form being: «أنا النذيرُ بعذابٍ مثلِ ما أنزلنا», even if the one who sends down is Allah, just as some of the king's intimates say «أَمَرْنا بكذا» ('we commanded such and such') though the king is the one who commands. As for the saying of Abū Muḥammad «وأَنْزَلْنَا عليهم كما أَنْزَلْنا عليك», it is an unarranged statement, and perhaps its original is «وأَنْزَلْنا عليك كما أَنْزَلْنا عليهم»; so the Shaykh corrected it. There is something to consider in this: how can that be implied when the Qurʾān speaks to the contrary, namely His saying {عَلَى المقتسمين}?"
The ninth: that it is attached to His saying {لَنَسْأَلَنَّهُمْ} [al-Ḥijr: 92], its implied form being: «لَنَسْأَلَنَّهم أجمعين مثلَ ما أَنْزَلْنا» (We shall surely question them all, like what We sent down).
The tenth: that the kāf is redundant, the implied form being: «أنا النذير المُبين ما أنزلناه على المقتسِمين» (I am the plain warner of what We sent down upon the divisors); this must be interpreted on the basis that «ما» is an object of «النذير» according to the Kufans, since they let a described adjective govern, or on the implication of a suitable verb, that is: «أُنْذِركم ما أنزلناه», as fits the Basran position.
The eleventh: that it is attached to «قل», the implied form being: «وقُلْ قولاً كما أنزَلْنا على المقتسِمين: إنك نذيرٌ لهم» (and say a saying, as We sent down upon the divisors: you are a warner to them); so the saying to the believers regarding warning is like the saying to the disbelieving divisors, lest you think that your warning of the disbelievers differs from your warning of the believers; rather you are, in the attribute of warning them, in one position: you warn the believer as you warn the disbeliever, as though He said: I am the plain warner to you and to others.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين جَعَلُواْ}: several aspects in it. The most apparent: that it is an adjective of «المقتسِمين». The second: that it is a badal (substitute) of it. The third: that it is an explicative apposition of it. The fourth: that it is accusative in blame (naṣb ʿalā l-dhamm). The fifth: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The sixth: that it is accusative by «النذير المبين»; al-Zamakhsharī said it, and it is rejected by the objection of an adjective governing while described, according to the Basrans, whose explanation was given earlier.
And «عِضين» is the plural of «عِضَة», which is a faction; so «العِضين» are the factions, and the meaning of their making the Qurʾān thus: some of them made it poetry, some sorcery and some soothsaying — we seek refuge in Allah from that. It was also said: al-ʿaḍh is sorcery in the language of Quraysh; they say «هو عاضِهٌ» and «هي عاضِهَةٌ». He said:
295 - 3- أَعُوذُ بربِّي مِن النَّافِثا ... تِ في عُقَدِ العاضِهِ المُعْضِهِ (I seek refuge in my Lord from the women who blow on the knots of the sorcerer, the sorcerer)
and in the hadith: «لَعَن العاضِهَة والمُسْتَعْضِهَة», that is, the female sorcerer and the one who asks for sorcery. It was also said: it is from al-ʿiḍah, which is lying and slander. It is said «عَضَهَهُ عَضْهَاً وعَضِيْهَةً», that is, he accused him of slander; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. It was also said: it is from al-ʿiḍāh, which is a thorny, harmful tree; al-Farrāʾ said it.
Regarding the final radical of «عِضَة» there are two views, each attested by morphology: the wāw, for their saying «عِضَوات», its derivation being from al-ʿuḍw (limb), because it is a part of a whole, and for its diminutive «عُضَيِّة»; and the hāʾ, for their saying «عُضَيْهَة» and «عاضِهٌ», «عاضِهَةٌ» and «عَضِهٌ». In the hadith: «لا تَعْضِيَةَ في مِيراثٍ», interpreted as: no division of what harms the heirs, its division being like a sword broken in two halves, so its value diminishes.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ʿiḍīn are parts, plural of ʿiḍa, whose original is ʿiḍwa, on the pattern fiʿla, from «عَضَا الشاةَ» when he made it into limbs. He said:
295 - 4- وليسَ دينُ اللهِ بالمُعَضَّى ... (The religion of Allah is not one to be cut into parts)
ʿIḍa was pluralised as ʿiḍīn, as were pluralised sana, thuba and ẓuba. Some of them make the nūn run with the vowels along with the yāʾ, as was explained earlier, and in that case its nūn is retained in annexation, so it is said «هذه عِضِيْنُك»."

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فاصدع}: the original of al-ṣadʿ is splitting: «صَدَعْتُه فانصَدَعَ», that is, I split it and it split; and from it comes also separation, as in His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ} [al-Rūm: 43].
He [the poet] said:
295 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كأنَّ بياضَ غِرَّتِه صَدِيعُ (... as though the whiteness of his blaze were the dawn-split)
Al-ṣadīʿ: the light of dawn, because the darkness splits from it; and the meaning of «فاصدَعْ» is: separate truth from falsehood and distinguish between them. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ṣadʿ is a split in hard bodies such as glass and iron; «صَدَّعْتُه» with doubling, so it splintered, and «صَدَعْتُه» lightened, so it split; headache (ṣudāʿ al-raʾs) is from it, because of the imagined splitting in it; and «صَدَعْتُ الفَلاةَ», that is, I crossed the desert, is from that, as though he imagined its being divided."
And «ما» in «بما تُؤْمَر» is maṣdar-forming or in the sense of «alladhī», the original being «تُؤْمَر به»; the omission of the preposition is regular with this verb, so omission of the returning pronoun is eloquent, and it is not like your saying «جاء الذي مررت». Similar is:
295 - 6- أَمَرْتُكَ الخيرَ فافعَلْ ما أُمِرْتَ به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (I commanded you the good, so do what you were commanded ...)
the original being «بالخير». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ما» may be maṣdar-forming, that is, «بأَمْرِك», a maṣdar of the passive." End [of the quotation]. This is sound speech. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] reported from him that he said: "The maṣdar may be intended for «أنْ» and the passive verb." Then the Shaykh said: "The sound view is that this is not permissible." I say: the disagreement is only about the explicit maṣdar: may it resolve into a maṣdar particle and a passive verb, or not? A well-known disagreement. As for whether the maṣdar particle may be followed by a passive verb, as in «يُعجبني أن يُكْرَمَ عمرٌو», or not, that is not the point of dispute.
